findings.title: A composed unit that faithfully paraphrases a SUPPORTED inherited_unit fact its own fact_ids cite - rather than quoting that fact verbatim - gets no refutation from either fold path, so a factuality/absence finding that misreads the paraphrase as unsupported or missing survives every check and blocks.
findings.detail: content_units.json's scope_limitations unit at slot 'limitation:2' (fact_ids: example:007, inherited_unit:046.paragraph, public_symbol:globaltransform) reads: 'Binary glTF export using binaryMode: true currently fails and throws a RangeError for any non-empty mesh, so only JSON/ASCII glTF export (the default, binaryMode: false) is supported.' inherited_unit:046.paragraph (SUPPORTED) is the upstream README's own verbatim text: 'Binary glTF (`.glb`, `binaryMode = true`) currently throws a `RangeError` for any non-empty mesh (...) Use the JSON/ASCII form (`binaryMode = false`, the default) shown above until that is fixed upstream.' - the same fact, correctly cited, faithfully paraphrased. Independent review's F03 calls 'JSON/ASCII glTF export (the default) is unaffected' absent and cites example:007 (SUPPORTED - the very example that runs this exact code path with binaryMode = false) for its factuality claim; its own review text admits 'which the candidate correctly notes but fails to emphasize as the recommended workaround' - not a missing fact, a de-emphasis complaint riding under the factuality criterion. Traced mechanically against scope_defect's fold stack (in call order): absence_defect requires the claimed-absent string to occur, under the same spelling rules that locate a quote, inside the candidate's own section slice - the candidate's paraphrase does not contain the string 'is unaffected', so absence_partition reports a real remainder and absence_defect returns None. Falling through to factuality_defect: unit_fact_ids correctly locates the unit and its citations (item 83's own widening, LANE-B-W14R3-F1), reviewed correctly includes inherited_unit:046.paragraph (kind inherited_unit, among unit_fact_ids), but _cited_literal requires the quote to contain the fact's own literal value as a contiguous substring after normalization - the candidate's sentence and the fact's sentence share meaning and cite the same evidence but not one matching run of text, so _cited_literal returns None and factuality_defect returns None: the finding is never folded, and it is not a reviewer-defect case built to be caught by any existing branch. repairs.json confirms this is not a fixable phrasing gap: the one repair attempt (b0e43fe2abafc344b9b794eb, label F03+F04) revised the neighbouring limitation:4 unit for F04 (a real fix, adm-zip reclassified) but left limitation:2's text completely unchanged for F03 - the model had nothing to correct, since the statement is already accurate - and the re-review (independent_review's second call this draw) re-raised F03 identically. Item 83 (LANE-B-W14R3-F1) closed the case where a reviewed unit's own inherited_unit citation is never checked at all; this is the same shape one level further - the citation is checked, but only by literal substring containment, which a legitimate paraphrase of an inherited fact never satisfies. Proposed, smallest first: widen _cited_literal (or add a sibling check reachable from both absence_defect and factuality_defect/cited_fact_defect) to treat a cited SUPPORTED fact as grounding a claim that substantially restates it - e.g. a normalized token-overlap or key-phrase containment test, not only contiguous substring containment - scoped exactly as _cited_literal already is, to the finding's own and the reviewed unit's own citations, never the whole fact set (the collision item 45 was written to stop).
